ios.desc:
Start with the photos. You'll look at them anyway. Photerra is a map of real photographs, not listings — every pin is a photo someone took standing there, so you can see what a place actually looks like, from where, and in what light. Google Maps tells you a place exists; Photerra shows you what it looks like from where someone stood.

EVERY PHOTO WAS TAKEN BY SOMEONE STANDING THERE
Not business listings. Not stock photography. Every spot on Photerra is a real photograph taken by a person who stood there — most by Photerra travelers, some drawn from open photo archives, each credited on the spot. The bench at sunset, the turn in the trail where the view opens up, the café with the good light. Every pin sits where the photograph was taken.

NO SPONSORED SPOTS. YOUR DATA STAYS YOURS.
Unlike travel apps built on advertising, Photerra has no sponsored spots and no paid placements — nobody pays to rank. When you book through a clearly labelled partner link we may earn a commission; that never touches the map. We never sell your data, and Quiet Mode lets you share spots and plan trips without putting your name on them.

SEE IT BEFORE YOU GO — IN THE RIGHT LIGHT
Most photographs carry the time of day they were shot, so you can filter the map by Morning, Afternoon, Golden hour, or Night. Chasing a sunset viewpoint or an early-morning trail? Find spots photographed in the light you're looking for.

A TRIP PLANNER THAT CAN'T INVENT A PLACE
Tell Photerra where you're going and what you like — "a weekend of quiet viewpoints in Portland," "three days of good food and long walks in Rome" — and it builds a day-by-day itinerary only from real photographed spots — nothing invented. An AI planner can send you somewhere that doesn't exist; this one can't, because every stop is a place someone photographed. Invite people and plan it together. If the planner puts it on your plan, someone stood there first.

ROAD TRIPS, PLANNED AROUND REAL SPOTS
Driving from A to B? Photerra strings photo spots along your actual route — the overlooks, pull-offs, and small towns worth stopping for — and splits them into days by drive time.

BRING IN A PLAN FROM ANYWHERE
Paste an itinerary from ChatGPT, Gemini or Claude, a booking email, or a link from Google Maps, TikTok or Instagram (Trips → Create → Bring in a plan from elsewhere), and Photerra turns it into a trip: every place goes on your map, with real photos where travelers have taken them, and a stop that can't be placed is kept by name,

quotes.text:
Quick links:

• Web: https://photerra.com.

• iOS: https://apps.apple.com/us/app/photerra/id1621490090.

• Android: https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=com.app.photerra.

• Privacy/Terms: https://photerra.com/privacy · https://photerra.com/terms.

One way to try it:

1. Install → sign in (Apple/Google/email).

2. Add spots from your camera roll (we read EXIF GPS) or drop pins manually.

3. Build a trip: drag spots into days, share with friends.

4. From your plan, open provider deep links to finish booking.

Or just explore: open the map and use the filter dropdown to browse seeded spots in your area.

For local exploring too!
You don't need a trip planned. Walk your neighborhood, save spots from recent photos, then tap any spot → "Open in Maps" or "Ride with Uber/Lyft." Fast way to turn "I should check that place out" into actually going.

Seeded areas (actively adding content):
San Francisco, Portland, San Diego, Los Angeles, Hawaii, Philadelphia, Yosemite & Sequoia National Parks, Mexico City. If you're local and want to help seed spots, reach out!

Known limitations:

• EXIF stripped? (common with cloud exports) → You can still add spots manually via map.

• Large photo dumps: Clustering is on; first load may take a moment on older devices.

• Offline maps and more export formats are on the roadmap.

Coming soon:

• Instant Add (bulk upload): Dump a backlog of photos and auto-create map spots in one pass (titles/categories are quick-editable). Shipping shortly; …
